slides.heading: Year 1 — Autumn 1, Week 1
slides.sub: New content taught directly, practised in words/sentences and applied in reading and dictation.

slides.heading: Mon
slides.objective: Learn the new sound "ay" (/eɪ/) and start reading and spelling words that use it.

slides.svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="-90 -110 180 180" width="320" height="320" role="img" aria-label="hay" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" class="wp-icon" data-picture="hay"><circle cx="-36" cy="-34" r="34" fill="#c99a63" stroke="#6d4318" stroke-width="3.5"/><path d="M-56.4 -34q20.4 -10.2 40.8 0" fill="none" stroke="#6d4318" stroke-width="2.5"/><path d="M-53 -19.72q17 -6.8 34 0" fill="none" stroke="#6d4318" stroke-width="2.5"/><circle cx="36" cy="-34" r="34" fill="#c99a63" stroke="#6d4318" stroke-width="3.5"/><path d="M15.6 -34q20.4 -10.2 40.8 0" fill="none" stroke="#6d4318" stroke-width="2.5"/><path d="M19 -19.72q17 -6.8 34 0" fill="none" stroke="#6d4318" stroke-width="2.5"/><circle cx="0" cy="-96" r="34" fill="#c99a63" stroke="#6d4318" stroke-width="3.5"/><path d="M-20.4 -96q20.4 -10.2 40.8 0" fill="none" stroke="#6d4318" stroke-width="2.5"/><path d="M-17 -81.72q17 -6.8 34 0" fill="none" stroke="#6d4318" stroke-width="2.5"/></svg>

slides.mnemonic: When the /ai/ sound comes at the end of a word, it packs its bags and wears its 'y' boots instead of its 'i' coat. Sunbeam Day always waves goodbye with a big 'ay!' as the sun goes down.

character.name: Sunbeam Day
character.blurb: Sunbeam Day is the last warm ray of sunshine at the end of a bright day, and she only ever appears at the end of a word, just like 'ay'.

slides.pronunciation_note: This is another way to write the same sound children already know as 'ai' in rain — 'ay' is usually used at the end of a word, like day and play.
slides.formation_cue: Write 'a', then 'y', close together — two letters, one sound.
slides.action: Children stretch both arms up like sun rays, then swoop them down and out to the side while saying 'ay!' as if waving the day goodbye.

slides.tip: Made of two words joined together — 'to' plus 'day' — so once you know both halves, the whole word falls into place.

slides.dictation: The band plays in the park.

slides.heading: Tue
slides.objective: Learn the new sound "ou" (/aʊ/) and start reading and spelling words that use it.

slides.svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 100 100" width="320" height="320" role="img" aria-label="cloud" class="wp-icon wp-raster" data-picture="cloud_a"><image href="data:image/png;base64," x="0" y="0" width="100" height="100" preserveAspectRatio="xMidYMid meet"/></svg>

slides.mnemonic: Boomer Cloud can't help it — every time he bumps into another cloud he lets out a great big 'ou!' that rumbles right across the sky.

character.name: Boomer Cloud
character.blurb: Boomer Cloud is a big grumbly cloud with one dark stripe across his middle, and he booms out 'ou' whenever he bumps into his friends.

slides.pronunciation_note: This is another way to write the same sound children already know as 'ow' in cow — 'ou' usually appears in the middle of a word.
slides.formation_cue: Write 'o', then 'u', close together — two letters, one sound.
slides.action: Children cup their hands round their mouth and call 'ou!' loudly like they're shouting across a playground.
slides.svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 100 100" width="320" height="320" role="img" aria-label="cloud" class="wp-icon wp-raster" data-picture="cloud_a"><image href="data:image/png;base64," x="0" y="0" width="100" height="100" preserveAspectRatio="xMidYMid meet"/></svg>

slides.dictation: A cloud drifts round the hill.

slides.heading: Wed
slides.objective: Learn the new sound "ie" (/aɪ/) and start reading and spelling words that use it.

slides.svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 100 100" width="320" height="320" role="img" aria-label="pie" class="wp-icon wp-raster" data-picture="pie_fc"><image href="data:image/png;base64," x="0" y="0" width="100" height="100" preserveAspectRatio="xMidYMid meet"/></svg>

slides.mnemonic: Clyde Owl only opens his big eyes at night, and when he does he blinks twice and hoots a soft 'ie'.

character.name: Clyde Owl
character.blurb: Clyde Owl has one soft feather tuft standing up between his round eyes, and he only calls out at night, just like the sound hiding inside 'ie'.

slides.pronunciation_note: This is another way to write the same sound children already know as 'igh' in night — 'ie' often appears at the end of a word.
slides.formation_cue: Write 'i', then 'e', close together — two letters, one sound.
slides.action: Children blink both eyes slowly, twice, while saying 'ie' softly like a sleepy owl.
slides.svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 100 100" width="320" height="320" role="img" aria-label="pie" class="wp-icon wp-raster" data-picture="pie_fc"><image href="data:image/png;base64," x="0" y="0" width="100" height="100" preserveAspectRatio="xMidYMid meet"/></svg>

slides.dictation: The pie has a sweet smell.

slides.heading: Thu
slides.objective: Extra practice blending and segmenting everything taught this week — no new content today.

slides.dictation: We play in the park at noon.

slides.heading: Fri
slides.objective: Revisit everything taught this week, read the matched decodable book, and check how securely it has been learned.

slides.dictation: A fork and a cup are on a tray.
